target_customer: Independent small and medium retailers in Brazil buying inventory, and the micro and small brands selling to them
problem: Independent retailers had difficulty finding new brands and buying inventory on credit, while small brands lacked an efficient route to retailers.
business_model: B2B wholesale marketplace with commission on completed sales and trade credit to retailers
product_category: B2B wholesale marketplace with trade credit

founders.name: Rodrigo Cruz
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is now working on something new in fintech.

founders.name: Guilherme Cruz
founders.background_notes: YC page says he changed careers about 10 years earlier to pursue programming.

founders.name: Bruno Passos
founders.background_notes: YC page: studied mechanical engineering, then became passionate about programming and joined after hearing Rodrigo's idea.

exit.reason: Not stated by the company; one e-commerce outlet says it closed its doors in Brazil in 2022

competitors.name: Wabi
competitors.what: Marketplace app for small neighborhood stores in Latin America, no merchant fees
competitors.traction_then: Present in seven Latin American countries in the later description

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace plus credit decisioning and supplier payouts in Brazil, built by a team of six listed on the YC page.

defensibility.rationale: Curated brands and credit relationships could create some stickiness, but the marketplace model was copyable and larger platforms targeted the same retailers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Wabi and brand-run platforms expanded in 2020 to 2021 per press; no source ties their moves directly to Gonddo's closure.

market_need_then: Brazil has about 5 million small and medium retailers per a founder quoted by Startups.com.br about a competitor, and 2020 to 2021 press describes many B2B marketplaces targeting them.

branding.domain_note: Used gonddo.com.br; the domain now redirects (301) to atacaly.com, a Brazilian platform connecting shopkeepers and suppliers whose relationship to Gonddo is not stated.

brand_strength.rationale: Only startup press about funding was found; no brand pages, interviews or community evidence exist in the sources opened.

outcome_analysis: One Brazilian e-commerce outlet reports that Gonddo stopped operating in Brazil in 2022, after a seed led by Iporanga in early 2021, but gives no cause and no other source confirms it, so the cause is not public. The company advanced supplier payments and offered retailers up to 60 days of credit, which tied up capital, but no source says this caused the closure.
notes: The seed amount of $0.6M and its date of 1 Feb 2021 rest on a single database (CB Insights); the press release and Startupi say the amount was undisclosed. TheCompanyCheck lists a $125K seed in June 2021 with Y Combinator, which matches the standard YC investment and is not recorded as a round. Startupi says an earlier first investment came in February of the prior year with no amount or investors, recorded as other. The shutdown date rests on one outlet. Competition evidence is limited to one source dated in 2020; Compra Agora and others surfaced without dated sources and are not listed.
